submitted.rationale: Index 10 (Cu0.35Sb0.65) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0365%. Its XRD shows near phase-pure trirutile CuSb2O6, which MACE puts on the convex hull. EQE fell on both sides of it: 0.021% at the Cu-rich mixed-phase index 4 and 0.012% at the Sb-rich CuSb2O6 + Sb-oxide index 13.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.021%. Mixed-phase film (CuSb2O6 + Cu-rich phase), and MEGNet predicts a narrow gap for Cu3Sb4O12.
Measured EQE 0.012%. Secondary Sb-oxide phase present; adding Sb beyond the 1:2 ratio reduced the EQE.

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts CuSb2O6 (trirutile, Cu:Sb=1:2) on the hull, so a phase-pure film is likely near index 10, and XRD at index 10 shows a clean rutile-type pattern. MEGNet's ~0 eV gap is a known underestimate for Cu2+ d9 oxides. Measured CuSb2O6 gaps are about 1.5-2 eV, well below the 3.2 eV illumination, so the gap prediction doesn't count against this candidate.

Mixed, mostly uninformative. MACE puts Cu3(SbO3)4 near the hull (0.033 eV/atom), so a Cu-richer ternary or a mixed phase is plausible between Cu 0.43 and 0.57. The Cu2SbO5 value of 1.16 eV/atom above hull looks like a relaxation artifact. XRD at index 4 shows extra peaks beyond trirutile. Given the low EQE at the CuSb2O6 end, I'm moving to the Cu-rich mixed-phase region to explore it.

Weakly against the Cu-rich side. MEGNet gives Cu3(SbO3)4 a small gap (0.5 eV), suggesting a narrow-gap, recombination-prone phase, which fits the lower EQE at index 4. The measured EQE rises from Cu-rich to CuSb2O6. XRD at index 13 shows CuSb2O6 plus a secondary Sb-oxide phase, which could form a beneficial heterojunction. I'm measuring on the Sb-rich side.
